notes: DOCUMENTED TARGET — NOT RECORDABLE, and deliberately carrying NO phases. agent_supports:partial / daemon_capability:n/a / driver_capability:n/a -> frozen. The target arc, if opencode ever raised a qualifying dialog, would be: presession proc-<PID> ready -> ses_ session ready (new session_id) -> working -> waiting entered while NO tool call is in flight -> working after the user answers -> ready, holding ready across a >=15s trailing idle. It is not written as phases because there is no drivable trigger to produce it and a spec with phases invites a recording that would assert the wrong thing. WHY: opencode's only blocking-dialog mechanism is Permission.ask, and every call site of it is inside a tool's execute (with tool:{messageID,callID} injected) except two. doom_loop ('Continue after repeated failures', shipped as doom_loop:"ask" in the default build agent) is raised from the case "tool-call" stream handler on the line AFTER the tool part is written at state.status="running" — a tool call IS in flight while its modal is held, which fails this row's acceptance criterion #2. workflow_tool_approval is genuinely tool-less (one batch approval before any pending call starts, no tool field on the request) but is installed only under `if (c instanceof zf)`, the workflow-provider model class, for which this host has no account. None of the four triggers the row names is reachable: PermissionConfig has no sandbox or network-egress key; no workspace/server trust prompt exists in the bundle; MCP elicitation is foreclosed because opencode constructs its MCP client with no capabilities argument and the vendored SDK throws 'Client does not support elicitation capability'; and the auto-mode/settings-review slot is filled by doom_loop. NOT an observability gap: daemon_capability is n/a, not incapable — if such a dialog arose, permission.asked would reach HandlePermissionPromptHook and state_classifier rule 0 (predicate: the bare bool m.PermissionPending, no tool dimension) would render it waiting, and permission.replied — published for reject as well as once/always — would carry the release back out. The sibling 2.26 cell, assessed record in the same pass, establishes that channel end to end. UNBLOCK: opencode declaring an elicitation client capability, or a workflow-capable provider configured on the recording host.
